pairs.difference: A: ball sits low on rippled sand with a flat banded dune backdrop. The camera is modest and the ball has margin around it. B: ball is tilted so the cap is off-axis, and it nearly fills the frame. The sand is softly blurred and the camera is higher.
pairs.fix: Keep the ball smaller in frame with clear margin. Use a modest camera height and a clearly defined ground and backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: shelf with brackets, a flat curved marquee and a plank wall. The layers are few and cleanly stacked. B: box frame with visible side pillars, a vignette, and the target and bear overlapping into a deeper stack of layers.
pairs.fix: Use fewer, flatter depth layers with no vignette. Keep frame and shelf at the same mild perspective as the target.

pairs.difference: A: the air-flow streaks and vent slats have scattered, inconsistent directions. The wall stripes, ceiling corner and unit converge at different rates. B: the unit, vent and moulding share one calm perspective.
pairs.fix: Make vent slats and wall stripes follow the same vanishing directions as the unit's edges. Draw the airflow as a few clean streaks.

pairs.difference: A: strongly top-down chest with the lid ellipse, bubbles overlapping the front, and a flat blue backdrop with sand only in the corner. B: sand runs back to a soft horizon, with a frontal chest face and a lid interior seen from a higher angle.
pairs.fix: Keep the chest front and lid interior at one camera height. Keep the background simple rather than adding a full receding sand ground.

pairs.difference: A: low camera, the cap rests on the planks, and the floor lines converge consistently. B: wall corner plus floor, and the visor brim flares up at the left edge so the cap looks half-floating. The badge is frontal while the body turns away.
pairs.fix: Rest the cap flat on the floor with the visor touching it. Use one clear camera angle for the badge, band and brim.

pairs.difference: A: booth with a cast shadow on a floor-wall split and a crown pattern behind. B: booth with soft grounding and a luggage pattern. Both show two faces at similar angles, and I see no clear viewpoint tell.

A: top-down view over wood planks that converge strongly, with striped wall behind. B: low camera with gloves filling the full width, overlapped in a tight, frontal crop. The cuffs are hidden or inconsistent.
pairs.fix: Show both gloves smaller in the frame with space around them. Keep one consistent camera height for both gloves and the table.

pairs.difference: A: fins foreshortened toward the viewer, with foot pockets and blades at the same tilt. B: large, near-parallel blades seen almost from above with pockets seen from the front, so the two parts don't share one view.
pairs.fix: Draw the foot pockets and blades from the same high three-quarter angle, with the fins foreshortened and smaller in frame.

pairs.difference: A: full scene with horizon, sky, water and beach, and a coherent dock. B: extreme close crop. The lifebuoy hangs in front of the post that passes through it, which confuses front-back depth.
pairs.fix: Show the whole dock at a moderate distance, with the lifebuoy hanging clearly in front of or beside the post.

pairs.difference: A: leaning trunk and fronds seen from the side, consistent with the dune. B: fronds splay out radially as if seen from above, while the trunk is seen from the side, so the view is mixed.
pairs.fix: Draw the crown from the same side-on angle as the trunk, with the fronds arching out and down.

pairs.difference: A: locker turned with a wall corner and baseboard, and planks that match its angle. B: a more frontal locker with wide fanning floor planks. I see only a weak tell.

A: spiral slide with a platform, a ladder in strong but consistent perspective, and a splash into the pool. B: the slide sweeps through the platform and ends in an open lip over the pool edge. The coil's depth doesn't resolve.
pairs.fix: Make the slide a clear spiral around the support. It should start at the platform top and end at the pool with water flowing out.

pairs.difference: A: tilted device with a readable top-and-front thickness and small earbuds. B: oversized, nearly frontal squircle with large foreground earbuds, which exaggerates the depth between them and the device.
pairs.fix: Make the earbuds smaller and in the same plane as the player. Show a clear top face and side thickness at one angle.

pairs.difference: A: flat, rotated top-down envelope with almost no perspective, like the real flat ticket card. B: a volumetric envelope with a thick body and an open flap seen in soft perspective.
pairs.fix: Draw the envelope as a flat top-down object, rotated in the plane, with minimal thickness and no perspective.

pairs.difference: A: low camera with a shallow plate ellipse, a striped wall behind, and a table: two backdrop layers like the real basket card. B: higher three-quarter view with a very large plate filling the frame and diagonal planks.
pairs.fix: Use a lower camera with a shallow plate rim. Add a wall-and-table backdrop and leave margin around the plate.

pairs.difference: A: door with a left jamb thickness, a wall sliver and dense foreground ivy. It has almost no straight edges detected, which fits painterly texture. B: arched door on a stone step with a clean frontal read.
pairs.fix: Reduce the foreground ivy overlap and keep the door face flat and frontal, with a clear step beneath.

pattern: Generated cards pick a camera angle for the whole hero and then break it in parts. Fins, palm crowns, slides and earbuds each show a different view. They also come out larger and tighter in frame than real cards, with a deeper or invented set of layers. Real cards keep one mild angle, simple layers and margin around the object.
